question.questionText: What causes the phases of the Moon?

referenceAnswers.referenceAnswer: The phases of the Moon are caused by the relative positions of the Earth, Moon, and Sun. As the Moon orbits the Earth, different portions of its sunlit surface are visible from Earth.

studentAnswers.studentAnswer: The Moon phases happen because the Moon orbits around the Earth and we observe different portions of the lit surface.
The Moon phases are caused by clouds in the Earth atmosphere blocking the Moon light at different times of the month.

question.questionText: Do heavy and light objects fall at different speeds in a vacuum?

referenceAnswers.referenceAnswer: No, in a vacuum where there is no air resistance, all objects accelerate and fall at the exact same rate regardless of their mass.

studentAnswers.studentAnswer: All objects experience gravitational pull in a vacuum, but heavier objects fall faster than lighter objects because they have more mass.
In a vacuum without air resistance, both heavy and light objects fall at the exact same rate.
